title: Semiconductor Supplier Delivery Risk
thesis: Every inbound shipment from a fictional Malaysian component supplier to an assembly and test plant either arrives by the PO commit date or it does not. Snowflake turns those shipments into on-time delivery and flag-precision KPIs, a 7-day delivery-miss risk score per supplier, ASN quantity variance anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Start with the question a plant buyer asks: how much of what our suppliers shipped arrived on time? 40 suppliers across 8 Malaysian cities, from Bayan Lepas and Kulim to Senai and Kuching, in 5 material categories.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to supplier-day rows.
The exception-signal chart shows which checks lead to confirmed delivery misses and which mostly produce false-positive flags.
show: Daily inbound shipments and exception flags
tabs.call_out: One governed definition of on-time delivery, from supplier dock to receiving

transition.line: Which suppliers should supplier quality call first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification ranks suppliers by the probability of a confirmed delivery miss in the next 7 days, so follow-up goes where it matters.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags ASN quantity variance outliers per supplier, and the forecast projects network-wide inbound shipments for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: Are supplier reviews and second sources keeping up?

talking_points: Supplier review completion, second-source coverage and qualifications still pending.
The scatter compares each supplier's review completion with its confirmed delivery misses.
tabs.call_out: Close second-source gaps before a capacity cut reaches the line

transition.line: What happens when a shipment arrives out of tolerance?

talking_points: Inbound-shipment events land in RAW.LIVE_SHIPMENTS: simulated in Snowflake, or from Amazon Data Firehose through S3 and Snowpipe in the AWS build.
FLAG events (a shipment whose ASN quantity variance is out of tolerance) are logged by the alert, which emails the supplier quality team.
tabs.call_out: From supplier dispatch to receiving alert in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent answers with generated SQL over the semantic view and cites the synthetic delivery-exception SOPs by ID.
The action memo is drafted only from KPI, supplier, exception-signal and risk rows; exception checks are demo signals, not supplier audit or qualification verdicts.
show: Agent answer with SQL and SOP citations
tabs.call_out: Answers carry their SQL and SOP IDs, so nobody has to trust a number blindly

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Both builds share the same core: seeded data, dynamic tables, Snowflake ML, Cortex Search, semantic view, agent, alert and task graph.
The AWS build adds Amazon Data Firehose, S3 and Snowpipe ingestion, a Bedrock memo and a QuickSight dashboard with an Amazon Q topic.
